question.problem: Find the equation of the tangent hyperplane to the hypersurface $w={x}^{2}+yz$ at the point $(-1,1,1,2).$
question.worked_solution:
The Cartesian equation of the tangent plane to the hypersurface $w=f(x,y,z)$ at the point $({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0},{w}_{0})$ on the hypersurface can be written as

$$
w-{w}_{0}=(x-{x}_{0})\frac{∂f}{∂x}({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})+(y-{y}_{0})\frac{∂f}{∂y}({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})+(z-{z}_{0})\frac{∂f}{∂z}({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0}).
$$

First, we find the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2}+yz)=2x \\ \frac{∂f}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{2}+yz)=z \\ \frac{∂f}{∂z} & =\frac{∂}{∂z}({x}^{2}+yz)=y\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we evaluate the partial derivatives at $(x,y,z)=(-1,1,1):$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x}(-1,1,1) & =2(-1)=-2 \\ \frac{∂f}{∂y}(-1,1,1) & =1 \\ \frac{∂f}{∂z}(-1,1,1) & =1\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we write down the equation of the tangent hyperplane:

$$
\begin{aligned}w-2 & =(x-(-1))\frac{∂f}{∂x}(-1,1,1)+(y-1)\frac{∂f}{∂y}(-1,1,1)+(z-1)\frac{∂f}{∂z}(-1,1,1) \\ w-2 & =-2(x+1)+(y-1)+(z-1) \\ w-2 & =-2x+y+z-4 \\ 2x-y-z+w+2 & =0\end{aligned}
$$
